title: NNTP CID extension suite: leaky content-addressing extensions
description:
Why: usenet-ipfs stores articles as IPLD blocks addressed by CID. Standard newsreaders never see this. But CID-aware tools (archival scripts, Corundum indexer, IPFS pinning automation) benefit from being able to discover and verify CIDs via NNTP without a separate API. These extensions are purely additive: they expose content-addressing metadata only, never topology or infrastructure state. Standard clients that never send an X command and never read X-Usenet-IPFS-* headers see zero behavior change.

Scope: five extensions across two categories —
  Passive (article headers): X-Usenet-IPFS-CID, X-Usenet-IPFS-Root-CID
  Active (X-commands): XCID, XVERIFY, ARTICLE cid:<cidv1>
All advertised in CAPABILITIES. All implemented in usenet-ipfs-reader.
design: Extensions categorized as: (1) passive headers added to ARTICLE/HEAD responses — zero protocol risk; (2) X-prefixed commands per RFC 3977 §7.2 — clients must explicitly opt in. Prohibited: topology, DHT, CRDT internals, pin/GC state.
